bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **SIP/systematic softness:** June systematic (SIP+STP) Rs 4,872 cr vs Rs 5,104 cr in March; net SIP trigger down as stoppages of old (performance-chased) SIPs exceed new adds — management calls it quality-of-sale, not structural, but a KPI to watch.
- **MTM dependence:** one-quarter market-share and other-income moves are MTM-driven (high equity base), so reported momentum flatters/hurts with the tape.
- **Debt-AUM outflows** on tight liquidity; **advisory AUM** shrinking with FII selling.
- **Regulatory yield pressure** (TER) — absorbed so far by passing to distributors; ongoing risk.
- **Alternates net yield volatility** (90-100 bps by mix); SIF still sub-scale (distributor exam barrier).
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Assured, long-horizon, candid; Nimesh Shah repeatedly deflects month-level and market-call questions ("see quarters, not months"; "let's discuss market views on the investor call") and frames product strategy as building track records for the future rather than near-term P&L. CFO precise on accounting mechanics (ESOP, Ventures restatement, seed capital).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The June "dip" is an MTM artefact + old-SIP churn**, not a demand break — new SIPs are still coming; the net trigger fell on stoppages.
- **ESOP + Q4 reversal, not real cost inflation**, explains the +14.3% QoQ opex — the June base is the clean run-rate.
- **Alternates AUM understates the franchise** — fee-earning AUM lags committed capital (drawn in tranches), so reported alternates AUM will step up mechanically as capital is called.
- **Debt-MF outflow is a corporate-liquidity signal** (war-driven working-capital redeployment), echoing the same macro MAHABANK cited for deposit softness.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Asset-light, high-return model: return on equity of 89.9% for the quarter versus 85.8% for FY26, with negligible finance cost.
- Treasury book of Rs 42,254.9 million as of 30 June 2026 is invested 72.9% in the company's own mutual funds, 23.5% in AIF, other equity and REITs, and 3.6% in corporate bonds — seeding and co-investment alongside customers.
- Within the mutual fund portion of investments, 57.1% sits in liquid and debt and 42.3% in equity and hybrid, indicating a liquidity-biased balance sheet.
- Cash was deployed inorganically for the ICICI Venture AIF management rights at a consideration of Rs 1,079.4 million.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Largest asset management company in India in active mutual fund QAAUM (13.3% market share) and in Equity and Equity Oriented Schemes QAAUM (13.6%) as of September 30, 2025 (CRISIL Report)
- Largest Individual Investor franchise — Individual MAAUM of Rs 6,610.3 billion, 13.7% industry share as of September 30, 2025
- Most profitable asset management company in India by operating profit before tax, with 20.0% market share for FY2025 (CRISIL Report)
- Leadership in Equity Oriented Hybrid Schemes with 25.8% QAAUM market share; consistent product innovation with the largest number of schemes (143) in the industry
- Pan-India multi-channel distribution: 272 offices across 23 states and 4 union territories; 110,719 MFDs, 213 national distributors, 67 banks including promoter ICICI Bank (7,246 branches)
- Strong promoter parentage — joint venture between ICICI Bank and Prudential Corporation Holdings since 1998; over 30 years of history and a trusted brand
- Modernised cloud-based technology stack, i-Invest app; 95.3% of mutual fund purchase transactions executed digitally in H1 FY26
- Experienced Key Managerial Personnel and Senior Management with average experience of over 25 years; risk-first investment approach aimed at long-term returns
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- AUM and management-fee sensitivity to markets and the economy — Fees are charged on assets managed or advised; adverse market or economic conditions, consumer confidence and household savings behaviour can reduce AUM and the management fees that form the bulk of revenue
- Revenue concentration in management fees — Management fees from mutual fund operations, AIF, PMS and advisory services were 89.0%-94.8% of revenue from operations across FY23 to H1 FY26 — a single dominant revenue driver
- Fee-mix dependence on equity-oriented schemes — Equity and Equity Oriented Schemes (55.8% of mutual fund QAAUM) generally carry higher fee structures; a mix shift toward lower-fee products would pressure the ~0.52% operating revenue yield
- Distribution dependence on third-party distributors and promoter ICICI Bank — MFDs (37.7%), national distributors (15.8%), ICICI Bank (8.3%) and other banks (11.1%) source the majority of Equity and Equity Oriented Schemes QAAUM; the company leverages promoter ICICI Bank's 7,246-branch network
- Untraceable historical corporate records — Certain corporate records relating to transfer of equity shares are not traceable; the Company cannot assure that no legal proceedings or regulatory actions will be initiated in relation to the untraceable filings, which may impact financial condition and reputation
- Reliance on commissioned third-party industry data — Market-share and industry-leadership claims rest on the CRISIL Report, which the Company commissioned and paid for; reliance on such information carries inherent risks per the DRHP's own risk factor
- Offshore advisory concentration within the Prudential group — The advisory business currently advises Eastspring, Prudential plc's asset management arm (advisory assets Rs 329.1 billion), tying that revenue stream to a single promoter-group relationship
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- **MF margins (annualised):** equity 66 bps, debt 32, liquid 12, passive 12, arbitrage 30.
- **Alternates:** gross yield 1.91%, **net yield 0.95%** (hovers 90-100 bps by mix); largest sleeve is long-only equity PMS + Cat-III AIF; Cat-II (private credit / commercial real estate) is debt-linked. Advisory yield 30 bps (international/FII-linked, AUM moderated on FII selling).
- **Debt MF:** QAAUM Rs 11.93 lakh cr, −6% QoQ — institutional redemptions as corporates redeployed surplus into working capital (war-driven), not seasonality.
- **Passive:** +25.3% YoY, boosted by gold/silver ETF inflows.

- **Distribution breadth** ("a supermarket": retail to HNI to family-office) plus falling TER as funds scale → SEBI's expense regime turned MFs into a **pull product** where scale compounds share.

business.body:
- Positions itself as one of India's oldest AMCs with over 30 years of history, incorporated in 1993, under an explicit 'Trust Compass' framing and an investment approach of managing risk first before aiming for long-term returns.
- Claims the highest industry market share in actively managed MF QAAUM (13.5%), equity schemes (14.0%) and equity-oriented hybrid (26.6%), with the second-highest share in total MF QAAUM (13.4%).
- Franchise breadth is presented across four businesses: mutual funds, portfolio management services, alternative investment funds and advisory services to offshore clients, spanning income accrual to long-term wealth creation.
- Alternates are positioned as a 'boutique within an institutional framework' — high-conviction portfolios backed by shared institutional fund management, research, risk and compliance, and sales infrastructure.
- ICICI Bank is disclosed as the holding company, yet ICICI Bank contributes only 7.7% of equity-scheme QAAUM distribution, indicating limited dependence on the parent channel.

business.body:

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: No plant or capacity expansion applies — the Company is an asset-light asset manager, and the Offer is entirely an offer for sale of up to 48,972,994 Equity Shares by Prudential Corporation Holdings Limited with no fresh issue, so the Company receives no proceeds to fund expansion. Growth is pursued organically: scaling the Alternates business (PMS, AIF, private credit, long-short, office yield funds and offshore advisory), a pan-India distribution network of 272 offices across 23 states and four union territories, and a re-engineered cloud-based digital platform (new websites, i-Invest app, enhanced distributor portal, fintech ecosystem integration).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management fees on AUM are the dominant revenue source — 92.7% of revenue from operations in H1 FY26 and 94.0% in FY25 (net of GST)
- AUM mix skewed to higher-fee Equity and Equity Oriented Schemes (55.8% of total mutual fund QAAUM as of September 30, 2025) supports operating profit; equity schemes generally carry higher fee structures than non-equity schemes
- Operating revenue yield stable at approximately 0.52% of AUM across FY23-H1 FY26; operating margin at 0.36%-0.37% of AUM
- Recurring systematic flows — SIP/STP inflows of Rs 48.03 billion for the month of September 2025
- Residual income from interest, dividend and net gain on fair value changes (7.3% of revenue from operations in H1 FY26, 5.9% in FY25) fluctuates with markets
- Return on equity rising from 70.0% (FY23) to 82.8% (FY25) and 86.8% annualised for H1 FY26

deepdive.thesis: A resilient Q1 for the #2 AMC: MTM recovery (small/mid-caps +24%/+17.2% vs large +8.9%) lifted equity AUM and drove PAT +23.1% YoY, while SIP/systematic flows dipped through Apr-May then rebounded in June — management insists the franchise is stable and stresses "look at quarters, not months." Core operating profit +20.2% YoY; **no negative TER impact** (passed to distributors). business_ops.supply_chain_integration: Asset management company (no physical supply chain); integration is through parentage and distribution. Operating since 1998 as a joint venture between ICICI Bank and Prudential Corporation Holdings Limited, the company leverages ICICI Bank's distribution network (7,246 branches across India as of September 30, 2025) and Eastspring's (Prudential's in-house asset manager, US$258.0 billion global assets as of December 31, 2024) multinational experience in fund management and distribution, including for the offshore advisory business. Multi-channel distribution as of September 30, 2025: 110,719 institutional and individual MFDs, 213 national distributors and 67 banks (including ICICI Bank) across 272 offices in 23 states and four union territories. Channel mix of Equity and Equity Oriented Schemes QAAUM as of September 30, 2025: MFDs 37.7%, national distributors 15.8%, direct sales 27.1%, ICICI Bank 8.3%, other banks 11.1%. Distribution is supported by a re-engineered cloud-based technology stack, the i-Invest app, distributor portal and fintech ecosystem integrations (95.3% of mutual fund purchase transactions executed digitally in the six months ended September 30, 2025). Investment management is conducted in-house with a research framework combining quantitative and qualitative analysis, an independent risk team reporting to the CEO, and a three-lines-of-control risk management structure (line management, internal controls/compliance, internal audit).

margins & cost dynamics: Operating margin 36.9 bps (vs 36.1 bps YoY) despite ESOP onset. Fee-&-commission (distribution cost for PMS/AIF) routed through the AMC and rising with alternates volumes — must be netted out to read the true expense base.
